worst_places.before: Secure (HTTPS only), HttpOnly (no JS access), SameSite=Strict (no cross-site requests) together block XSS via JS, CSRF via cross-origin isolation, and ensure encryption
worst_places.after: Secure (sent over HTTPS only), HttpOnly (JavaScript cannot read the cookie, so an XSS cannot steal the session), SameSite=Strict (the cookie is not sent on cross-site requests, which blocks CSRF) — together they limit what an XSS can do and block CSRF, but they do not prevent XSS itself

patterns: Abbreviation-first writing is the zone's defining habit: 140 unexpanded abbreviations across only 6.0k words of article prose (24.5 per 1k). The pattern is structural, not accidental — abbreviations are introduced in section HEADINGS ('## CIA Triad', '## Алгоритмы подписи — HS256 vs RS256', '## A10: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)'), where there is no room for a gloss, and then used freely in the body. 07-owasp-top-10.md and 08-security-interview-questions.md are the worst (13 and 21 flags in 295 and 670 words) because they are index/revision files that name every concept and explain none. Fix pattern: put the expansion in the first body sentence under each heading, not in the heading.

Sections systematically skip the lead sentence and open straight into a fenced block. 02 ('## Фундаментальное различие'), 03 ('## Access Token + Refresh Token'), 06 ('## Hashing vs Encryption'), 01 ('## HTTPS и TLS') open with a ```txt diagram; 07's A05, A06, A07 and A09 open with ```typescript. The reader gets the comparison table before being told what is being compared. This is why C averages 3.4 in a zone whose sentences (B 3.85) and examples (E 3.9) are otherwise strong: the language is clear, but the pyramid is inverted at section level.

The RU quiz bank is machine-translated where the RU question bank is hand-written, and they disagree on core terminology: 'prepared statements' is 'подготовленные выражения' in questions/security.json but 'подготовленные утверждения' in quiz/security.json; 'token' is 'токен' in half the quiz items and 'маркер' in the other half; 'output encoding and input validation' became 'кодирование выхода и валидацию входа'; 'defense in depth' became 'защиту в глубину'. Item 19 has a grammar error ('для кража кода авторизации'). The quiz is the only file in the zone scoring G=2.

The article's comment is also backwards on its own terms: 403 is the leaking response. (2) quiz item 25's correct answer says the cookie flags 'block XSS via JS', and item 13's explanation says 'HttpOnly prevents XSS from stealing the session token' — 04-xss-csrf-cors.md lists this belief under 'Типичные ошибки на интервью' and security-q-6 contradicts it directly. (3) quiz items 23/17/14 state flatly that 'CSP prevents XSS'; the article calls CSP 'последний рубеж обороны' and security-q-10 calls it 'a second layer of defense' — the quiz teaches CSP as a primary control.
